A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MagicPose4D and contain readable main text, equations, tables, and Appendices A and B. Matching the relocated material and figures supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction evaluations, motion-transfer and generation user studies, and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including keypoint-transfer accuracies in Table 2 and user-study results in Tables 1, 3, and 6.

M1.justification: The dual-phase reconstruction, global-local Chamfer loss, skeleton articulation, and motion-transfer procedure are unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that motion parameters come from reconstruction without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use DAVIS, PlanetZoo, DeformingThings4D, EverybodyDanceNow, and collected videos for the same reconstruction, generation, and motion-transfer tasks. Appendix A.3 and the motion scenarios in Table 5 are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and 6 and the qualitative comparisons. Reconstruction retains ViSER, LASR, LIMR, and S3O; motion transfer retains 3D-CoreNet and X-DualNet. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The keypoint-transfer metric, reconstruction without skeleton templates, training settings, and user-study procedures are unchanged. Sections 4.3 and A.4–A.5 retain the same evaluation designs and participant information.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Figure 6 retain the local Chamfer loss diagnostic, temporal-consistency comparison, and self-occlusion failure case. Appendix skeleton and skinning visualizations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean reconstruction accuracy over five runs in Section 4.3. Neither adds seed details, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–3 and 6 are identical, including MP4D's 74.2 average keypoint-transfer accuracy and 4.34 average motion-transfer rating. All twelve figure images also match exactly.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–9, including blend skinning, Chamfer losses, and appendix regularizers, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and concluding method summary retain the same claims about controlled 4D generation, dual-phase reconstruction, global-local alignment, cross-category transfer, and comparative performance.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the limitation concerning finger and facial motion with a warning that substantial skeleton or shape differences can produce unnatural transferred motion. It also proposes activity-level and primitive-activity-level transfer as future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 retains two NVIDIA L40S GPUs, batch size 16, ten epochs, learning rate 0.0001, and Zero123/SF3D usage. Project and supplementary-material links are unchanged; the new review link supplies no implementation information.

R1.justification: v3 adds two Chen et al. works to Section 2 and seven Haichao Zhang works through a citation cluster in Appendix A.5. These additions receive little explanation and do not substantially revise the research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 gains cross-references and small clarifications about reference-object reconstruction. The limitations paragraph is locally rewritten, and publication/review information is added. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds publication headers and changes placement, including moving Figure 2 from page 4 to page 5 and shifting appendix material. Figure images and table designs are retained; there is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies Section 3.3 and adds useful applicability guidance about dissimilar skeletons, but removes the explicit finger and facial motion limitation. Appendix A.5 also gains citations without explaining their connection to the study. With the methods and empirical support unchanged, it is unclear whether the clarification gains outweigh the lost disclosure and weaker citation integration.
